long_biography.plain_text:
Liberty Check Printers turned David L. Copham's production ideas into a business serving credit unions nationwide. His patents addressed how personalised checks could be printed, encoded, packed and prepared for delivery, linking mechanical workflow improvements to the company's core product. Liberty later broadened into cards, marketing, consulting, training and electronic banking services.

Harland acquired substantially all Liberty Enterprises assets for cash in 2005. The agreement covered equipment, inventory, receivables and intangible property as well as the operating business, and it listed trusts in Copham's and his wife's names among the controlling shareholders. After closing, Harland absorbed Liberty's product and service platform into its financial-institution business.
